decisive_items: CT and MRI of the head revealed a 30-mm mass lesion in the right temporal lobe
Whole-body PET-CT revealed increased uptake in the right axilla, anterior mediastinum, left pleura, and liver, consistent with cT4dN3M1 stage IV breast cancer
response.rationale: The new focal brain mass in a patient with HER2-positive stage IV breast cancer is most likely a brain metastasis, given the known CNS tropism of HER2-positive disease. The other candidates are either the pre-existing cancer stage, the primary diagnosis, or an adverse effect that would not produce a discrete 30-mm mass lesion.

rejected.why: Primary breast cancer is the original diagnosis, not the cause of the new brain mass.
Trastuzumab-related neurotoxicity would not typically manifest as a focal 30-mm temporal lobe mass and is far less likely than metastatic disease.
Stage IV breast cancer is already established from PET-CT and describes overall disease, not the new intracranial lesion.
